source: Minchat Shai on Gen 49:10 (the Ramah; the Masorah; the Zohar; Bachya)
claim_en: ad ki yavo SHILO ('until SHILOH comes' — the scepter clause): the most argued word in the testament, carried WHOLE — the WRITTEN form שילה with the yod AND the final he, exactly as the Ramah rules ('full yod, and it takes a he at the word's end'), as the Masorah counts, and as the Zohar reads it (yod-he); the READ form שילו with the vav — both forms unique in the Torah and both checked in-stream; MS calls the printed midrash-glosses that read it lean 'among the most astonishing errors,' and corrects the printed Masorah's own note (the true full-shilu stations are in Judges 21:21 and Jeremiah 7:12, named); Bachya (in his teacher's name) reads the accent on AD ('forever') as separating it from the coming — Onkelos' 'until Messiah comes' named; the counts (Shiloh = Messiah; = Moses, the Zohar's folio) named: the crux carried with every reading on file, the stream's letters checked.

source: the stream's own census on Gen 49:18 (the readings named)
claim_en: li-yshuatkha QIVITI YHWH ('For Your salvation I wait, O LORD'): the three-word cry — no mid-verse pause mark, the shortest verse of the testament — carries the LAST four-letter Name in the book of Genesis: the stream's own census finds NO Name-token after it, and only this one after the Potiphar span (39:23) — the Name that saturated the beginnings withdraws through the Joseph cycle and exits the book in the dying father's one interjection (asserted from the stream; the station checked); the readings hear Samson's serpent-rider fall and the cry between Dan's verses (named): the axis-verse of the poem.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 49:9 (the accents as arbiters; Sanhedrin and Tosafot named)
claim_en: mi-TEREF beni alita ('from the prey, my son, you went up'): MS settles the old debate (the Sanhedrin page on Judah and the blessing; Tosafot reading the Tamar confession — 'you lifted YOURSELF from the death-verdict'; Rashi and Ibn Ezra binding beni to alita) BY THE MARKS THEMSELVES: 'mi-teref carries the tifcha, WHICH DIVIDES; beni carries the connector, which does not' — the divider checked in-stream on the prey-word; and MS names the connector THE GALGAL (the rolling stroke) where SNAPSHOT writes the MUNACH: the run's SECOND galgal-vs-munach station (47:26 its twin) — the mark-split carried named, both strokes checked; the accents arbitrate the sentence: the son is bound to his rising, not to the prey.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 49:11 (the Ramah's exception-rule; the midrash named)
claim_en: osri la-gefen IRO... suto ('binding his FOAL to the vine... his GARMENT in the blood of grapes'): the vine-verse carries TWO written/read pairs — עירה and סותה both WRITTEN with the final he and READ with the vav (both pairs checked in-stream as their two tokens; the verse counts fourteen) — and the Ramah's rule marks the foal-word the Torah's EXCEPTION: every other word of its class is full with a final vav; this one alone full yod with the he; the midrash-chain reads the he as the city ('he shall bind Israel, the vine, to HIS CITY — Jerusalem'; the Yefe Toar and the readings named): the exception-letter carrying the city.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 49:13 (the Masorah's nine; Nehemiah named)
claim_en: ve-yarkhato AL tzidon ('and his flank UPON Sidon'): one of the Masorah's NINE presumed-until (sevirin) stations — readers presume AD ('unto Sidon'), the letter writes AL ('upon') and the Masorah locks it (MS pointing to the Nehemiah station for the file): the presumption-class of gen_69's four presumed-singulars gains its until-file — the letter checked in-stream against the reader's ear.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 49:21 (the Hilleli; the Ramah's mnemonic)
claim_en: ayala SHELUCHA ('a hind SENT FORTH' — Naphtali): LEAN in the Hilleli and all the books — and the Ramah's mnemonic seals the pair: 'one full and one lean — NAPHTALI'S is lean, ESAU'S is full': the census verifies EXACT — the full form stands ONCE in the whole Torah, at Esau's PRESENT (32:19, 'a present SENT to my lord'), and the hind runs lean (asserted): the gift-word fattened for the appeaser, thinned for the runner; Deborah's war and song named by the Kitzur (the hind = the ten thousand of Naphtali; the fair sayings = the Song, by count).

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 49:21 (his own collation; the Ramah found after)
claim_en: ha-NOTEN imre shafer ('who GIVES fair sayings'): the printed Masorah counts FIVE full giver-tokens and MS overrules it from the accurate books and manuscript Masorah-lists — FOUR full, ALL beyond the Torah (in the Psalms, named) — 'and my heart REJOICED in all my toil' (his own words) when he found the Ramah had ruled it before him: 'every giver-form in the Torah is written lean' — and the stream verifies the rule WHOLE: ZERO full giver-tokens in the Torah (the empty census checked), the lean pair standing at the hind's sayings and at 'who GIVES you strength' (Deut 8:18, from the stream): a scholar's joy, verified.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 49:3 (the Masorah's stressed pair; the stream's own pair)
claim_en: reuven BEKHORI ata ('Reuben, MY FIRSTBORN are you'): the my-firstborn word stands exactly TWICE in the Torah — Reuben's REVOKED one here and the NATION'S at the burning bush charge ('my son, my FIRSTBORN, Israel', Exod 4:22 — armed): the title stripped from the man is already the people's (census checked); and the Masorah's own pair is by STRESS — two fore-stressed my-firstborns: Reuben's and EPHRAIM'S ('Ephraim is my firstborn', Jer 31:9, named beyond the stream — the very son the crossed hands just installed): the fore-stress checked in-stream (the connector on the first syllable).

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 49:6 (the Masorah's pair; Isaiah named)
claim_en: bi-qhalam al TECHAD kevodi ('with their assembly let my honor not UNITE'): the unite-word's ONE Torah token (checked) — and its Scripture-partner is the tyrant of Isaiah, DENIED the union: 'you shall not UNITE with them in burial' (Isa 14:20, named): Jacob refuses the union of his honor with the plotters' assembly (the Kitzur: Korach's — that his name not be reckoned there even after death, and on the singers' rolls it is reckoned, named); the refused union and the denied one on one skeleton.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 49:6/15/26 (the maqqef rulings; the Scripture-three named)
claim_en: The maqqef file — MS rules three joinings 'with the maqqef, not with the lengthening-stroke,' and the stream writes ALL THREE: iqru-SHOR ('they hamstrung an ox', 49:6), le-mas-OVED ('a toiling serf', 49:15 — checked), ad-TAAVAT ('unto the desire of the everlasting hills', 49:26 — asserted): three hyphens ruled and found; and the serf-phrase's Scripture-three named by the Kitzur (Joshua's unexpelled Canaanites, Solomon's levy — Josh 16:10, 1 Kgs 9:21): Issachar's shoulder under the Torah's own hyphen.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 49:27 (the Hilleli; the Masorah's seventeen)
claim_en: BINYAMIN zeev yitraf ('BENJAMIN is a wolf that tears'): written FULL in the Hilleli and all the books — one of the Masorah's SEVENTEEN full Benjamins in Scripture (named) — and the stream's Torah-census closes the corpus's running file: SEVEN full Benjamins in the Torah, the naming (35:18), the not-sent (42:4), the prayer, the seeing, the greeted, the mouth-witness (45:12 — gen_68's sixth), and LAST the wolf-blessing (checked with all seven refs): the full spelling's Torah career ends at the tribe's own verse; the register-head lean (46:21, the census law) stands beside it — full for the person, lean at the muster.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 49:10/11/12/17/22/23/26/29 (the file; Or Torah)
claim_en: The pointing file: YIQHAT amim ('the obedience of peoples', 49:10) and IQVE sus ('the heels of a horse', 49:17) each with the qof DAGESHED 'FOR SPLENDOR' (MS's own term — a dagesh set for beauty, not grammar: the letters dressed for the poem; checked and asserted); KIBES ('he washes', 49:11) — most books point the bet SEGOL, Or Torah rules TSERE, and the stream writes the TSERE: with Or Torah against the many (checked); PORAT ('fruitful', 49:22) with the resh in QAMATS both times (most books, old prints, Or Torah); TIHYENA ('they shall be', 49:26) nun in QAMATS; NEESAF ('being gathered', 49:29) samekh in QAMATS per the Masorah (the Isaiah station named; asserted); the front-stroke on the alef of el ha-meara ('to the cave', 49:29), not on the he; VA-YEMARARUHU ('and they embittered him', 49:23) LEAN with the midrash's own lean-reading named; and CHAKHLILI ('darkened [eyes]', 49:12) — MS REJECTS the large-chet claim: absent from every manuscript and early print, absent from the printed Masorah's own large-letter list — a rejected crown carried as a rejection (named).

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 49:1/2/8/9/16/22/27/28 (named-only)
claim_en: The testament's number-crowns, carried NAMED-ONLY (letter-arithmetic and scroll-layout, not stream-marks): the hidden end — the sons answer that the letters of SIN do not appear in their names, and Jacob answers that neither do the letters of THE END (the concealment explained by the alphabet itself); the assembly-word holding the SIX words of the Shema ('Hear, O Israel' spoken to the father Israel, named); JUDAH'S verse (49:8) as a fixed COLUMN-HEAD of the Torah scroll — the yod of the six head-letters (with Bereshit's bet, the sea's he, the shin, the mem, the vav — the scribes' six, named: scroll layout, not stream); the David acrostics (the lion-whelp's initials; Dan 'as ONE of the tribes' = as David); ben PORAT = Manasseh-and-Ephraim by count (and 'the interpreting son' by sound-play); and THE SUN AND THE MOON: the initials following each son's name sum to 345 — the days of the SOLAR year — and the final letters of the blessings to 354 — the days of the LUNAR year — sealed by Jeremiah's covenant ('if these laws depart from before Me, the seed of Israel too shall cease', named): the twelve blessings counted against the two clocks; Dan-before-Gad here against Moses' Gad-before-Dan (buried in Gad's plot, named); and the VE-ZOT inclusio — the testament closes with the word Moses' blessing will open (Deut 33:1, armed): the stations checked, the arithmetic named.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 98:3
claim_en: THE DAILY LITURGY'S TWO OPENING LINES ARE SOURCED TO THIS DEATHBED - THE STRONGEST LITURGICAL CLAIM OF THE GENESIS WALK. 'Listen to Israel your father' (49:2) is parsed two ways, as 'listen to the GOD of Israel your father' and as 'your father Israel is LIKE a god.' Then Elazar ben Ahui derives the recitation itself: the patriarch asked his twelve sons whether any dissent was in their hearts, and they answered HEAR, ISRAEL - addressing their father by name - THE LORD IS OUR GOD, THE LORD IS ONE; and he replied with his lips BLESSED BE THE NAME OF HIS GLORIOUS KINGDOM FOREVER. Which is why, the passage says, Israel recites it morning and evening, addressing the patriarch in the cave: the matter you commanded us, we still practice. A twice-daily liturgical act, and the undertone line that accompanies it, both given their origin in a verse of this unit.

check.note: The Shema's recitation and its undertone response derived from a deathbed exchange, the verse's own address read as the sons speaking to their father by name.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 99:4
claim_en: THE BLESSINGS ARE DISTRIBUTED AND THEN POOLED, AND THE PROOF IS CHECKABLE IN OUR INK. The summary verse already says 'he blessed them,' so the chain presses the redundancy of 'EACH MAN ACCORDING TO HIS BLESSING he blessed them' and answers: having compared Judah to a lion, Dan to a serpent, Naphtali to a doe and Benjamin to a wolf, he then INCLUDED THEM ALL IN ONE ANOTHER'S BLESSINGS and made them all lions and all serpents. THE PROOF OFFERED IS MACHINE-CHECKABLE AND HOLDS: Dan is a SERPENT at 49:17 in this chapter and a LION'S CUB at Deuteronomy 33:22 in Moses' blessing - both in our own corpus, the same tribe carrying both images in the two blessings. A rule about how a whole set of blessings applies, resting on a cross-book pair we can verify.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 99:1
claim_en: THE SALE OF JOSEPH DISQUALIFIES ELEVEN TRIBES FROM THE SANCTUARY - THE FURTHEST CONSEQUENCE THAT ACT DRAWS IN THE WHOLE WALK. R. Akiva reads the contending mountains of Psalms 68:17 as THE TRIBES contending over where the Temple would stand, and has them told: you are all righteous, but you are all ‹גבננים› - THIEVES; every one of you took part in the sale of Joseph. But Benjamin, who did not, is 'the mountain God desired.' The site's title is thereby awarded by absence from a crime committed eleven chapters earlier. R. Yosei HaGelili reads the same verse of literal mountains told 'idolatry was done on your peaks,' and counter-readings by R. Yehuda and R. Shimon are recorded. The disqualification is not moralizing: it decides a location.

check.note: A sanctuary's location awarded to the one tribe absent from an earlier crime, the other eleven disqualified by participation in it.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 98:2
claim_en: THE CHAPTER'S GOVERNING CLAIM: THE END WAS REVEALED AND THEN SEALED. 'I will tell you what will BEFALL YOU AT THE END OF DAYS' draws three readings - Gog's downfall, the building of the Temple, and the Rabbis' answer that HE CAME TO REVEAL THE END AND IT WAS CONCEALED FROM HIM, proven by the fact that the next word out of his mouth is a son's name. That is the machine's reason this chapter is a set of blessings and not a schedule of dates. Only two are said to have had the End revealed and then withdrawn, this patriarch and Daniel. The 'gather and assemble' is opened four ways, closing with a command against dissension - you shall all be one assembly.

check.note: A prophecy of the end declared revoked mid-sentence, evidenced by the speaker's next word, explaining why the chapter is blessing rather than chronology.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 98:5
claim_en: THREE LAYERS STAND ON ONE VERSE, AND THE CHAIN PRESERVES THE RIVAL TRANSLATION'S DELIBERATE CHANGE. At 49:6 our ink reads 'in their anger they killed A MAN, and in their will they hamstrung AN OX ‹שור›' - both words verified in the corpus. The chain re-reads the ox as the WALL ‹שור› of the proselytes, making the massacre after the circumcision a damage to an institution rather than to a beast. AND IT RECORDS, BY NAME, THAT THIS IS ONE OF THE PLACES THE ELDERS ALTERED FOR KING PTOLEMY, writing the text so the king would not read the patriarchs as murderers. So three witnesses sit on this verse at once: our Hebrew, Onkelos - which narrates the incident into the verse and clears the father of it - and a rival Greek rendering preserved inside the midrash as a deliberate emendation. The two-shelves seam at its sharpest, and the tradition is the one keeping the record of the change.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 98:8
claim_en: THE SCEPTER IS READ AS AN INSTITUTION, AND A PHYSICAL DOCUMENT IS CITED AS EVIDENCE. 'The scepter shall not depart from Judah' is parsed institutionally - the scepter is the Sanhedrin that flogs and subjugates, the 'lawgiver from between his feet' the two scribes standing right and left of the judges, and the nations' submission read as the blunting of their teeth. Attached is a documentary claim of a kind this corpus rarely meets: A GENEALOGICAL SCROLL WAS FOUND IN JERUSALEM tracing Hillel to David, R. Hiyya the Great to a named son of David, and eight further houses to named ancestors. A standing rule supported by an artefact rather than by a verse, and the artefact is named as found.

check.note: A dynastic clause read as a judicial institution, supported by a genealogical document reported as physically found.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 100:2
claim_en: THE WILDERNESS CAMP'S FORMATION IS PREFIGURED BY A FUNERAL ORDER GIVEN AT THIS DEATHBED. Three commands are itemized - against idolatry, against blaspheming the Name, and the bearing of the bier: let no uncircumcised man touch it, and carry me THREE FROM THE NORTH, THREE FROM THE SOUTH, THREE FROM THE EAST, THREE FROM THE WEST - 'and just as you do for me, so you will be arrayed in four banners in the wilderness, with the Presence in the centre.' A standing arrangement of the nation claimed to originate in the seating of a coffin. Carried with a set of parallel deathbed instructions from later masters, including burial-garment customs and one who asked for staff and sandals so that if summoned he might rise ready.

check.note: A national marching formation claimed to originate in the ordering of pallbearers at a patriarch's funeral.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 99:9
claim_en: A STANDING INSTITUTION OF PATRONAGE IS SOURCED FROM THE ORDER OF TWO BLESSINGS. Zebulun is blessed before Issachar though born later, and the reason given is that Zebulun traded and Issachar studied, and Zebulun came and FED HIM - so precedence went to the supporter, on 'it is a tree of life TO THOSE WHO UPHOLD IT.' Moses' matching pair is cited as confirmation, with the tents belonging to the one who enables another to sit in them. The support-partnership between an earner and a scholar, one of the tradition's long-lived arrangements, is read out of nothing but the sequence of two verses.

check.note: A patronage institution derived from the inverted order of two brothers' blessings, the supporter placed first.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 100:1
claim_en: A WRITTEN-AND-READ PAIR CARRIED BOTH WAYS, WITH ITS INK DECLARED UNOPENED HERE. The chain builds on a verse whose word is written with one letter and read as another, taking the WRITTEN form in one master's hand ('He made us and NOT we ourselves,' set against Pharaoh's boast of self-creation) and the READ form in another's ('He made us and TO HIM we belong'). Both are kept. DECLARED UNOPENED: the verse is in Psalms, outside this Torah-only corpus, so the machine cannot inspect the written-and-read pair the argument turns on - it carries the claim on the chain's authority and says so. The same section counts this unit's 49:33 among three command-verses, and those three ARE in our ink, at 49:29, 49:33 and 50:12.

check.note: A written-versus-read pair argued both ways; the verse lies outside this corpus, so the ink is declared unopened and the claim carried on the chain's authority.

source: Onkelos Genesis 49:10; Onkelos Genesis 49:27; Onkelos Genesis 49:13
claim_en: THE TRANSLATION CHANGES GENRE IN THIS CHAPTER - THE LARGEST TRANSLATION-LAYER FINDING OF THE GENESIS WALK. Through forty-eight chapters Onkelos translates, deviating only at named points that this corpus has recorded one by one. Here it becomes an INTERPRETIVE PARAPHRASE: nearly every blessing is rendered as its historical or messianic meaning rather than its words. 'Until Shiloh comes' becomes 'until THE MESSIAH COMES, FOR HIS IS THE KINGSHIP.' Benjamin the ravening wolf becomes 'THE DIVINE PRESENCE WILL DWELL IN HIS LAND, AND IN HIS INHERITANCE THE TEMPLE WILL BE BUILT; in the morning and toward evening the priests will offer the sacrifices.' Seven consecutive middle blessings are rendered as their fulfilments - conquests, territories, a chosen man of Dan whose terror falls on the Philistines, two tribes from Joseph's sons. This is a fact about the reading shelf itself, not about a verse: the declared translation stops being a translation for the length of one chapter, and any weight this project puts on it as a witness must be adjusted here and nowhere else.

check.note: The declared translation shifts from rendering to interpretive paraphrase for the length of one chapter, altering its evidentiary weight as a witness.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 98:19
claim_en: THE SLANDER MODEL THE CYCLE OPENED WITH IS GIVEN ITS FULLEST STATEMENT AT THE CYCLE'S END. 'They embittered him and SHOT at him' is counted three ways - a son who embittered his brothers, a son whose brothers embittered him, a son who embittered his master's wife - and the verse is made to settle which was worst by the choice of verb. Then the teaching: why are slanderers likened to ARROWS rather than any other weapon? Because every other weapon strikes near and this strikes far - evil speech spoken in one country kills in another. And the broom-bush coals: all other coals die from within, these burn on inside though quenched without - so one who receives evil speech, even appeased, still burns within. The model opened by the three reports at the start of the Joseph cycle, stated in full at its close.

check.note: A model of slander as a long-range weapon and as coals that burn after quenching, closing a thread the cycle opened.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 99:11; Bereshit Rabbah 98:14
claim_en: A MESSIANIC EXPECTATION IS MOVED OFF ONE TRIBE ONTO ANOTHER BY ONE WORD, AND BOTH POSITIONS STAND. One reading maps Dan's serpent clause onto Samson line by line - found among women as the serpent was with Eve, restrained by oath as the serpent by charm, all his strength in his head, his venom killing more after death than before - and explains the cry that interrupts the blessings, 'FOR YOUR SALVATION I HOPE,' as the patriarch seeing Samson, taking him for the deliverer, then seeing that he would die. The other reading redirects: THIS one will not bring salvation; it will come from GAD, because 'he will raid at their HEEL ‹עקב›' is read to the one who comes AT THE END ‹בעקב›, the prophet Elijah, held to be of that tribe. The same interrupting cry, two destinations, and the corpus carries both without ranking them.

check.note: An interrupting cry for salvation read as disappointment in one tribe's deliverer and as redirection to another tribe's, both preserved.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 98:11
claim_en: A PROPHET'S PARENTAGE IS DECIDED BY ONE WORD OF THIS BLESSING. Two masters disputed Jonah's tribe - one proving him of Zebulun from his town's position in that lot, the other of Asher from the Sidonian town he was sent to - and the resolution reads this unit's own clause: 'his ‹ירכתו› shall be upon Sidon,' where the word is heard as the THIGH ‹ירך› from which he came. So his father was of Zebulun and his mother of Asher, and both proofs stand. A genealogical ruling extracted from a geographic phrase in a tribal blessing, settling a dispute about a book four centuries downstream.

check.note: A prophet's paternal and maternal tribes settled by reading a geographic term in a blessing as an anatomical one, reconciling two proofs.
